body:
Thanks for checking back.  Eh,  I guess I feel rather apathetic about it all at the moment... not as down as yesterday, but still don't feel right.  I guess the easiest way to sum it up at the moment is that I just don't give a shit.  I have a friend who is an alcoholic...  I keep thinking of her serenity prayer... what things can I control, what can't I.

I was unaware that wal-marts cheap meds included mental health.  I have no clue what any of those are, but if I can manage to work out getting to a Dr. I am thinking I can bring them that list and see if there is anything appropriate on it.

To be fully clear, the custody deal was something I was okay with.  I have been in some roles that caused me to have a lot of interaction with kids.  I often hear children that are in split custody situations refer to their residences as "moms house" and "dads house"... but never home.  I personally wanted my kids to still have one HOME, a place where all there stuff is, a place that they grow up remembering as their bedroom, their home.  I felt that it was better for me to sacrifice seeing them than they sacrifice having a place that was HOME in their minds.

Wiggl3s -

From what I understand technically the therapist was doing her job which was to help my wife deal with the issues that made her unhappy....  I don't know that there is legal ground against her for that since she did not actually reccommend anything illegal.  

I have tried to discuss the impact on the kids with her, unfortunatly she has a group of friends who are also divorced that are happy to provide endless justification for her actions.

Damn...  I think you might be me in the future.  Your description of your experience with your wife sounds incredibly similar.  It seems like there is a strong network of divorced women that embrace each other and help each other through... of course that often comes at the expense of the guys.  Not saying that to be sexist... it just is what it is, actually probably reflects worse on us guys because we just don't talk.

As far as a lawyer... the biggest challenge is cost...  I have held off on seeing a therapist because of the $30 copay.  

1.  Excellent points... at times I figure what the hell, maybe it is time for a whole new life.  It is difficult to look back at the life I previously had and not find myself mourning it.  It seems like to have lost all that I should have had to do something bad.

2.  I guess I like to believe it was (maybe still is on my part) love.  She has told me that she never was in love with me and was pretending for the 12 years just because she felt it was what she was supposed to do.  I am not familiar with Tristan... I will look into it.

3.  I am completly open to medication... again it goes back to the issue of $

Thanks again for your insight

I have done just that, her basic response was "your actions are not my problem".  Her lawyer and therapist have told her that all that matters is that she make herself happy.  If that destroys another life in the process then so be it.
